questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Beginners must apply concrete security defaults to container specs, learn how policies gate PRs, and validate locally and in CI.

## Key Concepts
- Kubernetes securityContext fields
- Kyverno policy syntax and testing
- CI gate integration in GitHub Actions

## Code Example
```yaml
apiVersion: kyverno.io/v1
kind: ClusterPolicy
metadata:
  name: require-sec-context
spec:
  validationFailureAction: enforce
  rules:
  - name: require-sec-context
    match:
      resources:
        kinds: ["Deployment","StatefulSet","DaemonSet","Job","CronJob"]
    validate:
      message: "Containers must run as non-root with readOnlyRootFilesystem and drop ALL capabilities"
      pattern:
        spec:
          template:
            spec:
              containers:
              - securityContext:
                  runAsNonRoot: true
                  readOnlyRootFilesystem: true
                  capabilities:
                    drop: ["ALL"]
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you adapt this policy for InitContainers? 
- How would you measure policy coverage over time (e.g., CI reports, dashboards)?

```yaml
apiVersion: external-secrets.io/v1alpha1
kind: ExternalSecret

  name: db-credentials
```

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Tests understanding of namespace isolation and basic egress filtering using NetworkPolicy. It checks hands-on ability to craft minimal, enforceable rules and verify them.

## Key Concepts
- Kubernetes NetworkPolicy basics
- Namespace-scoped isolation
- Egress rules and default deny
- Basic verification via kubectl and logs

## Code Example
```yaml
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: test-egress-isolate
  namespace: test
spec:
  podSelector: {}
  policyTypes:
  - Egress
  egress:
  - to:
    - ipBlock:
        cidr: 10.1.2.3/32
    ports:
    - protocol: TCP
      port: 443
  - to:
    - namespaceSelector: {}
      podSelector:
        matchLabels:
          app: dns
    ports:
    - protocol: UDP
      port: 53
  - to:
    - ipBlock:
        cidr: 0.0.0.0/0
        except:
        - 255.255.255.255/32
    ports:
    - protocol: TCP
      port: 53
```

```yaml
# Compliant Pod in test namespace
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: compliant-pod
  namespace: test
spec:
  containers:
  - name: app
    image: busybox
    command: ["sh", "-c", "sleep 300"]
```

```yaml
# Noncompliant Pod in test namespace (tries to access prod)
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: noncompliant-pod
  namespace: test
spec:
  containers:
  - name: app
    image: busybox
    command: ["sh", "-c", "wget http://prod.svc.cluster.local || true"]
```

```yaml
# DNS test Pod (for compliance with DNS allow rule)
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: dns-test
  namespace: test
spec:
  containers:
  - name: app
    image: busybox
    command: ["sh", "-c", "nslookup kubernetes.default.svc.cluster.local"]
```

## Follow-up Steps
- kubectl apply -f policy.yaml
- kubectl apply -f compliant-pod.yaml; kubectl exec compliant-pod -- curl logs.internal:443
- kubectl apply -f noncompliant-pod.yaml; observe failure to reach prod
- Check events: kubectl describe networkpolicy/test-egress-isolate -n test

## Why This Is Asked

Tests understanding of policy as code, basic Kubernetes security posture, and simple automation.

## Key Concepts

- Kyverno policy definitions
- Pod securityContext fields
- Image provenance enforcement

## Code Example

```yaml
apiVersion: kyverno.io/v1
kind: ClusterPolicy
metadata:
  name: secure-pods
spec:
  validationFailureAction: enforce
  rules:
  - name: ensure-secure-context
    match:
      resources:
        kinds: [Pod]
        namespaces: [secure]
    validate:
      message: SecurityContext must be non-root, readOnlyRootFilesystem, no privileged, drop ALL
      pattern:
        spec:
          containers:
          - name: "*"
            securityContext:
              runAsNonRoot: true
              runAsUser: 1000
              allowPrivilegeEscalation: false
              readOnlyRootFilesystem: true
              capabilities:
                drop:
                - ALL
  - name: image-policy
    match:
      resources:
        kinds: [Pod]
        namespaces: [secure]
    validate:
      message: Image must come from allowed registry
      pattern:
        spec:
          containers:
          - image: example.com/secure/*
  - name: image-pull-policy
    match:
      resources:
        kinds: [Pod]
        namespaces: [secure]
    validate:
      message: imagePullPolicy must be Always
      pattern:
        spec:
          containers:
          - imagePullPolicy: Always
```

- How would you test policy enforcement with a compliant Pod? a noncompliant Pod?
- How would you extend to cover initContainers or multiple namespaces?

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked

This checks practical CI gating for namespace discipline and Helm workflow. It exercises a concrete validation using YAML parsing and shows how to tie environment mapping to PR gates.

## Key Concepts

- Kubernetes namespaces
- Helm charts values.yaml
- YAML parsing with yq
- GitHub Actions gate
- Environment-specific deployments

## Code Example

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
ENV="${ENV:-dev}"
for f in manifests/**/*.yaml; do
  NS=$(yq e '.metadata.namespace // ""' "$f")
  if [[ -z "$NS" || "$NS" != "$ENV" ]]; then
    echo "Namespace mismatch: $f -> '$NS' (expected '$ENV')"
    exit 1
  fi
done
```

```yaml
# failing manifest (namespace: default)
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: example
  namespace: default
spec:
  template:
    spec:
      containers:
        - name: app
          image: example/app:latest
```

```yaml
# passing manifest (namespace: prod)
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: example
  namespace: prod
spec:
  template:
    spec:
      containers:
        - name: app
          image: example/app:1.0.0
```

## Follow-up Questions

- How would you adapt this for Helm templating where namespace is templated via release namespace?
- How would you scale the gate to multi-repo repos or different tooling (Kustomize, Skaffold)?

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked

Tests ability to implement a basic software supply chain gate: SBOM generation and vulnerability scanning integrated into CI, with clear pass/fail criteria.

## Key Concepts

- SBOM generation with Syft
- Vulnerability scanning with Trivy
- GitHub Actions workflow basics
- Exit-code driven gates and report interpretation

## Code Example

```yaml
name: SBOM and vulnerability gate
on:
  push:
    branches: [ main ]
jobs:
  scan:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - name: Build image
        run: docker build -t service:latest .
      - name: Generate SBOM
        uses: anchore/syft-action@v0
        with:
          image: service:latest
      - name: Trivy scan
        uses: aquasecurity/trivy-action@v0
        with:
          image: service:latest
          severity: HIGH,CRITICAL
          format: table
          exit-code: 1
```

```dockerfile
# Failing Dockerfile (vulnerable)
FROM debian:stretch-slim
RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y curl
```

```dockerfile
# Passing Dockerfile (secure, updated base)
FROM debian:bullseye-slim
RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y curl
```

## Follow-up Questions

- How would you adjust thresholds for different environments?
- How would you add caching and parallel scans to speed up CI?

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Tests ability to enforce secure secret handling across multi-cloud clusters, using policy-as-code, and integrating cert-manager with GitOps pipelines.

## Key Concepts
- Policy as code (Kyverno/OPA)
- cert-manager Certificate -> Secret flow
- ExternalSecret / SecretStore integration
- CI gating and canary verification

## Code Example
```yaml
# Kyverno policy (example)
apiVersion: kyverno.io/v1
kind: ClusterPolicy
metadata:
  name: deny-inline-tls-and-enforce-secretref
spec:
  validationFailureAction: fail
  rules:
  - name: deny-inline-tls
    match:
      resources:
        kinds: ["Deployment", "StatefulSet"]
    validate:
      message: "TLS data must come from cert-manager SecretRef; do not inline certificates"
      pattern:
        spec:
          template:
            spec:
              volumes:
              - secret:
                  secretName: "?!*"
```

```rego
# OPA/ValidatingAdmissionPolicy (illustrative)
package kubernetes.admission

deny[{"msg":"inline certs not allowed"}] {
  input.request.kind.kind == "Deployment" or input.request.kind.kind == "StatefulSet"
  some i
  secret := input.request.object.spec.template.spec.volumes[i]
  secret.secretName != "" # ensure SecretRef used, not inline data
}
```

```yaml
# Failing manifest (inline cert example)
apiVersion: v1
kind: Secret
metadata:
  name: tls-secret
type: kubernetes.io/tls
data:
  tls.crt: LS0tLS1CRUdJTiBDRVJUSUZJQ0FURS0tLS0t... # inline cert data
  tls.key: LS0tLS1CRUdJTiBSU0EgUFJ...
```

```yaml
# Passing manifest (SecretRef to cert-manager Secret)
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
spec:
  template:
    spec:
      volumes:
      - name: tls
        secret:
          secretName: my-cert-manager-secret
```

```yaml
# CI validation steps (high level)
- lint manifests
- run policy gate (Kyverno/OPA) on PR
- validate that Deployment references cert-manager Secret (no inline data)
```

```yaml
# ConstraintTemplate
apiVersion: templates.gatekeeper.sh/v1beta1
kind: ConstraintTemplate

    spec:
      names:
        kind: K8sApiConstraint

        }

          pod.metadata.annotations["spiffe.io/spiffe-id"]

        }
```

## Why This Is Asked
Tests basic manifest linting and security checks in CI.

## Key Concepts
- Kubernetes manifests
- YAML parsing with yq
- GitHub Actions gating
- SecurityContext and imagePullPolicy

## Code Example
```yaml
# .github/workflows/ci-manifest-gate.yml
name: Manifest Gate
on: [pull_request]
jobs:
  gate:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - name: Validate manifests
        run: |
          set -e
          violations=0
          for f in $(git diff --name-only origin/main | grep -E '\\.ya?ml$' ); do
            if ! yq e '.spec.template.spec.containers[].readinessProbe' "$f" >/dev/null 2>&1; then violations=$((violations+1)); fi
            if ! yq e '.spec.template.spec.containers[].livenessProbe' "$f" >/dev/null 2>&1; then violations=$((violations+1)); fi
            if ! yq e '.spec.template.spec.containers[].securityContext.runAsNonRoot' "$f" | grep -q true; then violations=$((violations+1)); fi
            if ! yq e '.spec.template.spec.containers[].securityContext.runAsUser' "$f" | grep -q '1000'; then violations=$((violations+1)); fi
            if ! yq e '.spec.template.spec.containers[].imagePullPolicy' "$f" | grep -q 'Always'; then violations=$((violations+1)); fi
          done
          if [ "$violations" -gt 0 ]; then exit 1; fi
```

```yaml
# failing.yaml (no readiness/liveness probes or runAsNonRoot)
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: bad-app
spec:
  replicas: 1
  template:
    spec:
      containers:
        - name: app
          image: example/app:latest
          imagePullPolicy: IfNotPresent
```

```yaml

apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: good-app
spec:
  replicas: 1
  template:
    spec:
      containers:
        - name: app
          image: example/app:latest
          imagePullPolicy: Always
          securityContext:
            runAsNonRoot: true
            runAsUser: 1000
          readinessProbe:
            httpGet:
              path: /health
              port: 80
          livenessProbe:
            httpGet:
              path: /health
              port: 80
```
